title: In the summer the bowl in which
instructions: is made should stand in ice while the process is going on. The old time-devouring way by dropping the oil with one hand and stirring with the other has happily been obviated by various oil dropping inventions which have reduced the work to a minimum. The housekeeper is often puzzled to know what to do if the quantity of mayonnaise needed is too much for one raw yolk and not sufficient for two. By mashing a hard cooked yolk with the raw yolk the problem will be settled. The process of making is the same as if both yolks had been uncooked. They are first seasoned with salt and white pepper and mustard if it is wanted. Then the oil is dropped slowly while the beating continues rapidly.
As the eggs begin to thicken drops of vinegar or lemon juice are added from time to time.
